rules.rule: 1. One event log and no second store: any file outside app/lib/spine/ that imports a storage driver fails the build
rules.evidence: app/test/persistence_boundary_test.dart:8-29 walks every .dart under lib/, skips lib/spine/, and fails on an import or export of sqflite|drift|hive|hive_flutter|shared_preferences|sqlite3|sqlite3_flutter_libs|idb_shim|idb_sqflite|sembast|isar|objectbox|realm or of dart:indexed_db|dart:html, in either quote style. I probed it rather than read it: appending `import "package:hive/hive.dart";` to app/lib/flags.dart made the test fail with `storage drivers may only be imported under lib/spine/: [lib/flags.dart]` (persistence_boundary_test.dart:28); the file was restored and `git diff --stat -- app/lib/flags.dart` is clean. A second test (persistence_boundary_test.dart:31-41) keeps the drivers under lib/spine/store/ only, and the drivers do live there: app/lib/spine/store/store_native.dart, store_sqlite.dart, store_web.dart. Two holes the rule as written does not cover, neither of them presently exploited: `package:web` (pubspec.yaml:41) reaches window.localStorage without importing dart:html, and plain dart:io file writes are not matched — app/lib/media/local_uri_io.dart:20-29 writes blob bytes into getTemporaryDirectory() from outside lib/spine/. That one is a derived cache keyed by the spine's own content hash (video_player needs a file URI), not a second source of truth.

rules.rule: 2. At least fourteen event types, docs and code agreeing, each with a thread rendering, a notification treatment and a search behaviour, and a test asserting the same list
rules.evidence: app/lib/spine/types.dart:85-242 declares eighteen EventTypeSpecs, each carrying renderer, notify (types.dart:13-22) and search (types.dart:25-36). docs/EVENT_TYPES.md rows 33-50 list the same eighteen ids in the same order; docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:52 says "Eighteen types. The floor is fourteen." app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:8-18 parses the doc table and asserts `expect(documented, registered)` plus >=14 and no duplicates. The renderer end is held at both sides by app/test/thread_types_test.dart:16-30 (every type names a renderer in kThreadRenderers, every renderer is named by a type), the sentence end by thread_types_test.dart:32-72 (summaryOf is non-empty, is not the registry id, contains no underscore and no ISO timestamp for every type), and the notify/search end by app/test/floors_test.dart:84-95. Rendering, notification and search are all driven off the one registry rather than off private switches: app/lib/regions/chat/renderers.dart:338-360, app/lib/regions/settings/notifications.dart:44-47, app/lib/spine/search.dart:31-84. Two blemishes, both cosmetic: app/lib/spine/types.dart:1 still says "the same seventeen types" when there are eighteen, and app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:21-25, named 'every required type from the brief is present', lists seventeen and omits `passed_on`.

rules.rule: 3. A fifth shared-life module is a directory plus one line; the commit that added the fourth touched nothing under the first three
rules.evidence: The registry half is true: app/lib/modules/registry.dart:10-16 is a five-entry const list and app/lib/regions/us/us_region.dart:40-52 iterates it, so Us picks a new module up with no edit (the per-module row count at us_region.dart:69-73 has a `_ => 1` default, so it is not a required touch). The modules are genuinely decoupled — nothing under modules/dates, modules/todos, modules/calendar or modules/rituals mentions shelf or `passed_on`. But the fifth module did not cost one line. `passed_on` also required app/lib/spine/types.dart:218-225 (registry entry), app/lib/regions/chat/renderers.dart:354 (renderer map) and :401 (the summaryOf sentence), app/lib/material/assignment.dart:31 (paper stock) and docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:48 — five shared files outside modules/shelf/, four of them source. The claim in app/lib/modules/registry.dart:1-2 and app/lib/modules/module.dart:4-5 ("a directory under modules/ and one line here: nothing under the existing modules changes") holds only for a module that reuses an event type that already exists. The commit-level half of this rule I did not check: I was instructed not to read the build history, so I can state the structural coupling but not what any particular commit touched.

rules.rule: 4. Typing and presence ticks are never events and never reach the log
rules.evidence: Typing goes out as an Ephemeral, a type that is explicitly not an Event: app/lib/transport/transport.dart:131-141, sent at app/lib/scope.dart:174-176 and received at scope.dart:153-161 with a six-second self-expiry. The host hands an ephemeral frame to a callback and never to the spine (app/lib/transport/protocol/server_io.dart:227-232; contrast _push at :209-225 which calls spine.accept). transport.dart:127 says these are "never stored" and app/test/transport_local_test.dart:207-222 asserts it end to end: a 'typing' frame client→host and a 'presence' frame host→client both arrive, and `expect(r.host.length, 0); expect(r.client.length, 0)`. No `append`/`emit` call site in app/lib names a typing or presence type — the full set emitted is message, photo, video, voice_note, reaction, message_edit, message_delete, read_marker, feeling, state_declared, state_passive and the five module types.

rules.rule: 5. Read markers are never rendered as rows in the thread
rules.evidence: app/lib/spine/spine.dart is the only writer of read markers (app/lib/scope.dart:185). The projection consumes one into a per-person high-water mark and returns before `_add`: app/lib/spine/projections/thread.dart:272-278, and only types with rowInThread reach _add at thread.dart:280-281. app/lib/spine/types.dart:153-161 sets rowInThread: false for read_marker (and :131 for reaction, :141 message_edit, :151 message_delete). The renderer it names is honest about being unreachable — app/lib/regions/chat/renderers.dart:347 maps 'ink_dries' to `_neverARow`, a SizedBox.shrink documented at renderers.dart:110-113. Asserted at app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:31-34 and app/test/thread_types_test.dart:96-104, and the read marker's real effect (rows turning `read`) is exercised at app/test/scroll_cost_test.dart:130-141 and app/test/reliability_test.dart:81-85.

rules.rule: 6. No secret in any committed file — TS_AUTHKEY, a CA private key, a pairing secret — in history as well as the working tree
rules.evidence: Working tree: every hit for TS_AUTHKEY|tskey-|AUTHKEY|pairing_secret is the name of an environment variable or prose about it — bootstrap.sh:12,217-221, tools/tailscale/up.sh:48-51,107-109 (which passes --authkey="$TS_AUTHKEY" from the environment on the process command line and writes only the word "supplied" to toolchain/ts/AUTHKEY_STATUS), README.md:23. .gitignore:12-16 excludes .env, *.authkey and /toolchain/ts/. History: rather than read the log, I enumerated every object in .git with `git cat-file --batch-all-objects` — 3314 blobs, i.e. the content of every file ever committed — and grepped each for `tskey-…`, `-----BEGIN … PRIVATE KEY-----` and `privkey:…`. Zero hits of any kind. The only key-shaped strings anywhere in the tree are the two `nodekey:` values in evidence/coldstart.json, which are Tailscale *public* node keys out of `tailscale status --json`. The app never loads a private key: the single SecurityContext reference (app/lib/transport/protocol/server_io.dart:53) is a pass-through of an object the binding supplies, and no binding supplies one. Caveat: this scans file content, which is what the rule asks about; commit messages were out of scope for me.

rules.rule: 7. The host binds only its tailnet address and refuses any request not authenticated with the pairing key
rules.evidence: The binding half is the strongest thing in the transport. app/lib/transport/tailscale/tailnet.dart:22-33 defines a tailnet address as 100.64.0.0/10 or fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48 and nothing else; addressToServeOn (tailnet.dart:56-71) checks a declared address rather than trusting it and throws NotOnTheTailnet when there is none — there is no fallback branch. app/lib/transport/tailscale/tailscale_transport.dart:72-79 is the only producer of the HostBind, and app/test/tailnet_test.dart:20-43 asserts that 0.0.0.0, 127.0.0.1, 192.168.0.10 and :: are all refused as declared addresses, with tailnet_test.dart:64-69 refusing an off-tailnet peer on the client side too. Authentication of the API is real: server_io.dart:87-93 reads the body, parses the Authorization header and 401s before routing, and _authenticated (:119-130) checks the paired client id, a ±kAuthSkew timestamp, an HMAC over method+path+query+ts+nonce+body with a constant-time compare, and a nonce cache against replay; app/test/transport_local_test.dart:70-86 asserts an unpaired pull throws and that the wrong six words do not pair. Where it falls short of the rule as stated: server_io.dart:80-83 routes every path that does not start with kApiPrefix ('/v1', wire.dart:9) to _serveStatic *before* any authentication, which contradicts the file's own header at server_io.dart:2-3 ("Every request except the two pairing calls must carry a valid pairing signature"). I tested the obvious escape and it does not exist — _serveStatic (:274-280) normalises and rejects a leading '..', and dart:io parses a `GET //etc/passwd` target as authority 'etc' path '/passwd', which I confirmed with a live HttpServer, so p.join stays under the root. The exposure is therefore the PWA bundle itself, to any unpaired peer that can reach the port, and it is inert in the shipped app because main.dart never passes pwaRoot — only app/tool/host_daemon.dart:67,94-98 does, driven by capture.sh:176. Which is the other half of the gap: the app has no path that serves the PWA at all, so the Apple half of the brief is served today by a development daemon. Finally, no run in evidence has actually bound a tailnet address — evidence/reliability.json tailscale.host_listener and evidence/coldstart.json host_listener both read "127.0.0.1:8443", honestly explained (userspace tailscaled has no TUN) and narrower rather than wider, but the phone path is held only by unit tests.

rules.rule: 8. Every file in assets/ has an entry in assets/MANIFEST.json naming its generator, and no asset or font was downloaded from the internet
rules.evidence: I walked assets/ myself: 698 files, of which 696 have an entry in assets/MANIFEST.json. The two that do not are sidecar metadata, not assets — assets/sound/MANIFEST.sound.json and assets/tears/relief.json. All 707 entries carry a `generator`, and every distinct generator is a script in this repository: blender/folds/fold.py (245), blender/objects/objects.py (141), blender/paper/tear_relief.py (113), tools/tears/tear.py (57), blender/paper/stocks.py (54), blender/bits/bits.py (44), tools/sound/synth.py (44), tools/handwriting/build.py (5), tools/ink_plate.py (2), blender/shell/desk.py (2). The two hands are built, not fetched: assets/fonts/NoorHand.ttf and TeoHand.ttf are generated by tools/handwriting/build.py from tools/handwriting/hands.json and skeletons.json, whose sha256s are recorded in the entry for assets/fonts/MANIFEST.fonts.json. No curl, wget or http(s) fetch of an asset appears anywhere in tools/ or blender/ (the only https strings are tailscale's login URL and a push endpoint example). The seed media is the same story — seed/MANIFEST.json names tools/voice/say.py and friends. One blemish: eleven manifest entries name files that are not in assets/ and never were, absolute build-scratch paths of the form ../../../tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/obj_test/obj_candle.png. tools/check/manifest.py sees them — evidence/logs/manifest.json lists them under entries_without_a_file — and passes anyway.

rules.rule: 9. The tests pass, and they test what they claim to
rules.evidence: They pass: `flutter test` from app/ ran 107 tests to `All tests passed!` with exit code 0. Most of them have real teeth, and several are property tests over the source rather than over a fixture — I verified persistence_boundary_test by breaking the source (see rule 1), and nothing_moves_on_the_wall_clock_test.dart:27-68, nothing_is_set_in_an_icon_font_test and nothing_is_drawn_by_the_diagnostic_test.dart:45-57 (which reads the decoration the framework actually resolved, not what the widget asked for) are the same shape. scroll_cost_test.dart:147-165 does the thing its name implies and more: it asserts the incremental projector's rows, order, text, edits, reactions, delivery and read markers equal the from-scratch projection at every 997th prefix of a 14006-event year. reliability_test.dart:279-283 asserts all seventeen capabilities rather than only reporting them. Two tests are weaker than their names on any machine where the tailnet daemons are down, which is this one: 'reliability report over the tailscale transport' (reliability_test.dart:296-345) and 'cold start over the tailnet: four events, both directions, both spines agreeing' (coldstart_test.dart:68-104) both return early after writing status "pending", executing zero assertions, and are counted among the 107 passes. The pending is recorded honestly in the artifacts — evidence/reliability.json tailscale.later_check.status and evidence/coldstart.json later_check.status both read "pending", over an earlier run dated 2026-09-05 that did assert — but a green suite here is not evidence of a tailnet. Smaller: spine_schema_test.dart:21-25 omits passed_on from the list its name calls complete (harmless, the docs-equality test covers it), and app/lib/spine/projections/thread.dart:159 cites a test file, thread_incremental_test, that does not exist in app/test/ — the coverage it names is real but lives in scroll_cost_test.dart.

findings.where: the module registry and the four shared files a new module's event type has to touch
findings.what: A fifth shared-life module is a directory plus one line only if it reuses an event type that already exists; the fifth one that shipped, shelf, also required app/lib/spine/types.dart:218-225, app/lib/regions/chat/renderers.dart:354 and :401, app/lib/material/assignment.dart:31 and docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:48.
findings.why: The brief's structural test of extensibility is exactly this cost, and registry.dart:1-2 and module.dart:4-5 both state the one-line claim in the source, so the code asserts something about itself that the code does not do.

findings.where: the passive half of the partner-state signals
findings.what: kPassiveSignals declares battery, charging, last_active, local_hour, ringer, moving, network and at_home, but the only writer of a state_passive event in the whole app is app/lib/capture/hooks.dart:74, which is compiled in only when Flags.capture is set (app/lib/capture/hooks.dart:33-38); there is no platform channel, no sensor plugin in app/pubspec.yaml:30-45, and the rest of these signals exist only in the seeded year (seed/tools/finish.py:161-197).
findings.why: "Each person's inner state is continuously legible to the other" is the mission's second half, and on a real phone nothing produces that state — every passive fact in the evidence is seeded or harness-driven, which the pictures cannot distinguish from a running nervous system.

findings.where: the push response, and what the client does with it
findings.what: The host's push reply is a list of {'id','seq'} only, and app/lib/transport/protocol/http_transport.dart:215-217 parses only those two, so Accepted.refused (app/lib/transport/transport.dart:113) is always null, the refusal branch at app/lib/transport/sync.dart:108-113 is unreachable over the wire, and an event the host drops as invalid (app/lib/spine/spine.dart:246-247, a bare `continue`) is simply absent from the reply — it stays in the outbox, is re-pushed on every sync, and shows as sending or queued forever with no mark and no record anywhere.
findings.why: Delivery.refused is one of the five delivery states the thread draws (app/lib/spine/projections/thread.dart:12-27, app/lib/regions/chat/note.dart:312) and the only production caller of markRefused is the capture staging at app/lib/regions/chat/chat_region.dart:143, so 13_messenger_states.png shows a state the transport cannot produce while the real failure it stands for is silent.

findings.where: the request router, above the authentication check
findings.what: Every path that does not begin with '/v1' is handed to _serveStatic before any pairing signature is checked, which contradicts the file's own header at server_io.dart:2-3; it is inert in the app because main.dart never sets pwaRoot, and live in every harness run that passes --pwa (capture.sh:176 into app/tool/host_daemon.dart:94-98).
findings.why: Rule 7 says the host refuses any request not authenticated with the pairing key, and a comment claiming a stronger rule than the code enforces is the kind of drift the rest of this build guards against with tests.

findings.where: the two tailnet tests, and coldstart_test.dart:68-104
findings.what: Both return early with status "pending" and execute no assertions when the daemons are not answering, yet are counted among the 107 passing tests; 'cold start over the tailnet: four events, both directions, both spines agreeing' asserted nothing in this run.
findings.why: A test that asserts nothing while its name claims a crossing is exactly the weaker-than-its-name case rule 9 names, even though the pending state is recorded honestly in evidence/reliability.json and evidence/coldstart.json.

findings.where: eleven entries naming files outside the tree
findings.what: The manifest carries absolute build-scratch paths such as ../../../tmp/claude-0/.../scratchpad/obj_test/obj_candle.png that correspond to no file in assets/ and never did; tools/check/manifest.py reports them under entries_without_a_file in evidence/logs/manifest.json and passes anyway.
findings.why: The manifest is the record of where every asset came from, and a record that names eleven things that do not exist is a record nobody has read.

findings.where: the registry's own header, and two test names
findings.what: types.dart:1 says docs/EVENT_TYPES.md "lists the same seventeen types" when there are eighteen (docs/EVENT_TYPES.md:52); app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:21-25, named 'every required type from the brief is present', lists seventeen and omits passed_on; app/lib/spine/projections/thread.dart:159 cites thread_incremental_test, which does not exist (the coverage is in app/test/scroll_cost_test.dart:147-165).
findings.why: Three comments that describe a state of the code one step behind the code, in the files whose whole job is to be the single place a type is declared.

what_is_working: The one-log rule is enforced by a test with teeth rather than by convention: I broke it on purpose (an added hive import in app/lib/flags.dart) and app/test/persistence_boundary_test.dart:28 failed the run with the offending path named.

Eighteen event types, with docs/EVENT_TYPES.md rows 33-50 and app/lib/spine/types.dart:85-242 held to the same list in the same order by app/test/spine_schema_test.dart:8-18, and rendering, notification and search all read off that one registry (renderers.dart:338-360, notifications.dart:44-47, search.dart:31-84) with app/test/thread_types_test.dart holding both ends of every mapping.

Typing and presence are a separate wire type that the host never hands to the spine, and app/test/transport_local_test.dart:207-222 proves it by asserting both spines are still length 0 after a frame has crossed in each direction.
Read markers, reactions, edits and deletes all fold into the row they point at, with a renderer that is explicitly a no-op (renderers.dart:110-113) rather than an accidental blank.
The tailnet binding is one function with no fallback branch, and app/test/tailnet_test.dart:20-43 asserts that 0.0.0.0, loopback, an RFC1918 address and :: are each refused even when declared.
The API is signed rather than merely bound: HMAC over method, path, query, timestamp, nonce and body with a constant-time compare and a nonce cache (server_io.dart:119-130).

3314 blobs — every version of every committed file — scanned for auth keys and private keys with zero hits; the only key material anywhere is a pair of public Tailscale node keys in evidence/coldstart.json.
707 asset entries, every one naming a generator script inside this repository, including both handwriting fonts, which are built from local skeleton JSON whose hashes are recorded.
107 tests pass, and an unusual number of them are source-level property tests that would catch the class of regression they name rather than a single instance of it.
The incremental thread projector is proved equal to the from-scratch projection across a 14006-event year (app/test/scroll_cost_test.dart:147-165), so the one-log rule costs nothing at scroll time.
verdict: Read as source rather than as pictures, this is a coherent build with a real spine: one append-only log, a storage boundary that I verified fails the build when crossed, eighteen registry-declared event types whose thread rendering, notification treatment and search behaviour are all read off that single declaration and held there by tests at both ends, ephemeral typing and presence that provably never touch the log, read markers folded into a high-water mark instead of drawn as rows, a tailnet bind with no fallback path, and not one secret in any of the 3314 blobs the object store holds. Where it falls short is on its own claims about itself. The headline extensibility promise — a fifth shared-life module is a directory and one line — is written into two source files and is true only for a module that reuses an existing event type; shelf cost four source files and a doc row outside its own directory. The passive half of the emotional nervous system has no producer on a device at all: every battery, ringer and at-home fact in the evidence comes from the seed or from a capture-only hook, so what the artifacts show as continuous legibility is, in the code, a fixture. And the delivery-refusal path is a fiction end to end: the wire has no field for it, the client's refusal branch is unreachable, an event the host rejects vanishes from the reply and is re-pushed forever unmarked, and the one place a refusal is ever drawn is the capture staging that produced the messenger-states artifact. None of that is blocking — the architecture would take a sixth module, a nineteenth event type or a second transport without rework, which is what the row is for — but three structural claims in this build are currently stated rather than met, and that holds it at its floor rather than above it.
